requiredFindings.title: The link reader crosses member custody-state and VCS anchors
requiredFindings.problem: The link loop excludes inner repository/project boundaries but never applies the admitted member’s pruning anchors before _link reads a provider manifest. A literal workspaces entry a/.opensip/p admits a and returns a link from a/.opensip/p/package.json, even while the provenance marks a/.opensip as an opensip-custody-state pruned tree. A literal a/.git similarly returns a link from a/.git/package.json. SX-1 makes the member-root .opensip an exact never-entered anchor, and item 21 admits only the specified three member Git objects before C1. The current reference therefore uses bytes its own discovery scope excludes.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Apply the owning anchor/read-boundary rules before consulting descendant placement/provider bytes. Do not read or link a provider under M/.opensip or a pruned VCS tree. Preserve membership-by-placement independently where lawful, and select a justified existing disclosure or obtain the needed narrow law/registry decision rather than inventing a public reason. Add Cargo and npm regression cases with an observation/read spy that proves the hidden manifest is never consulted.
evidence: A supplied-content get spy recorded /h/w/a/.opensip/p/package.json, and discover returned ACCEPT with packageName=hidden, providerMember=/h/w/a and packageDir=a/.opensip/p.
A separate a/.git entry returned ACCEPT with packageName=git-hidden and packageDir=a/.git.
The resulting provenance still reports the same directories as opensip-custody-state/vcs-tree anchors.

requiredFindings.title: Branch A skips earlier grammar/absence failures before returning a member failure
requiredFindings.problem: Invalid root grammar and missing roots are deferred to pass two, while later candidate layout, volume, cap or 6b failures can return immediately. This contradicts LD-B3B0-6’s stated grammar-and-absence-first order and changes the earlier SLM refusal. Mixed-failure arrays are absent from the checker.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Validate the array’s grammar and existence in the intended order before candidate-specific terminal decisions, preserving the appropriate owning SLM refusal/path/detail. Do not merely return every pass-one refusal: ordinary member crossings are precisely what this wrapper must resolve. Add mixed-failure controls with invalid/missing roots and otherwise independently failing member candidates for both config roots and explicit joins. If a different public priority is intended, settle and document that decision instead of claiming the current stated order.
evidence: configWorkspaceRoots=["../bad","a"] with a holding a .git file: pass one refuses PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID/JOIN_PATH_GRAMMAR, but discover returns PROJECT.ROOT_CUSTODY_REFUSED/member-vcs-unsupported:git-not-directory.
configWorkspaceRoots=["missing","a"] on the same tree: pass one refuses PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID/ABSENT, but discover returns the later member-layout refusal.

requiredFindings.title: VCS side-table evidence is not carried into selection and boundary discovery
requiredFindings.problem: _markers uses vcsMarkers to decide W2 and placement, but base drops that side table without projecting its positive observations into the legacy fs VCS evidence. _finish then feeds that unchanged representation to B2-b0/SLM. Under the documented side-table interface, a directory with a positive .hg side-table observation and no legacy vcs flag is excluded as a member but is not recorded as a nested repository; its package is discovered as an ordinary unit. One positive VCS fact is thus used for exclusion and ignored for the boundary it must preserve.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Define and enforce one consistent VCS observation representation before pass one and pass two. Project side-table markers into the legacy selection/population evidence, withholding that evidence only for admitted members, or reject an incomplete/inconsistent observation before discovery with a documented input contract. Add side-table-only .hg/.svn/.jj and .git-file cases, including root/ancestor selection, excluded candidates and nested repositories inside admitted members. An excluded repository must remain a boundary and its contents must not become ordinary units.
evidence: A synthetic /h/w/a with a physical .hg directory, vcsMarkers={"/h/w/a":[".hg"]}, and no legacy vcs flag produces member-excluded/member-vcs-unsupported:vcs-other for reader entry a.
The same result has nestedRepositories=[] and includes /h/w/a as a workspace-auto unit, despite that positive VCS observation.
The input API documents vcsMarkers as carrying VCS information not expressed by the legacy single flag; no consistency requirement is validated.

requiredFindings.title: The member depth limit is incorrectly imposed on the declaring entry
requiredFindings.problem: _place rejects any declaring entry directory deeper than 256 segments as entry-path-absent before locating its candidate. Law item 19 M1 bounds the member M’s depth, while the registry’s entry placement requires the actual directory to exist without links/device changes; it does not impose this limit on D. A shallow member can therefore disappear solely because its declaring package directory is deeper. Native walker depth behavior is not authority to report an existing reader entry as absent or change membership-by-placement.
requiredFindings.requiredChange: Apply M1’s depth bound to the candidate member, separately from any owning rule for the declaring entry or provider read. Preserve the shallow candidate’s lawful declaration. If a depth restriction/disposition for reader entries is wanted, obtain an explicit law/registry decision and cite it. Replace LD-B3B0-3’s unsupported entry-depth rule and add boundary cases distinguishing candidate depth from entry depth.
evidence: A conventional member a at depth 1, declared solely by an existing package directory at depth 256, is admitted and linked.

Moving only that provider/entry directory to depth 257 produces members=[], no link and entry-path-absent, although the candidate remains at depth 1, every segment is a directory on the same device and the entry spelling is canonical.
The 257-segment example is only 513 ASCII path bytes, so this is not the schema’s string-length limit.
